claim.explanation: The route reads ' sun' and ' rises'. Early heads (L1-L5) bind the subject ' sun' to the motion verb ' rises', and L5/N2218+ fires on that sun-motion context and most strongly at the final ' the' after ' rises'. A distributed band of mid and late heads (L6-L19, notably L14/H7, L14/H2 and L18/H4) moves the verb identity (rises, not sets) to the final position. The final-layer heads L23/H1 and L23/H6 and the pole L23/N2505- write ' east'. Measured with the corpus means: mean-ablating the route cuts about 54% of the all-unit cut, the route alone brings back about 55%, and patching from 'The sun sets in the' moves about 82% of the gap and from 'The city lies in the' about 79%. Swapping ' sun' for another rising body keeps ' east'. Swapping ' rises' for a setting verb turns it to ' west'.
